newsitem.title: USA: Europe to grow faster, Japan perking up - IMF chief.
newsitem.headline: Europe to grow faster, Japan perking up - IMF chief.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus Sunday forecast faster economic growth in Europe next year and said that would help the drive to launch a single currency there in 1999.
"The recent rebound in the German economy is particularly encouraging," he told the IMF's policy-making Interim Committee.

He also sounded hopeful about the Japanese economy, which has only recently begun to show signs of snapping out of years-long stagnation. "In Japan, there are indications that the recovery has become more securely established," he said.
Camdessus said industrial countries have had success in fighting inflation and called that a "major achievement."
"The enhanced credibility of monetary authorities has provided some room for monetary policies to facilitate economic recovery in countries with large margins of unused resources," he said.

"But we must not be complacent about inflation now that it seems to be under control, and monetary authorities must remain alert to the possible need to take preemptive action where there is a threat of increasing inflationary pressures," he added.
